description: Synthetic-by-construction corpus for end-to-end retrieval and RAG evidence attribution evaluation. Expanded interaction version with at least ten labelled pairs per complementary, redundant, and conflicting relation.

passages.title: 2008 Summer Olympics host
passages.text: The 2008 Summer Olympics were hosted by Beijing, China.

passages.title: Opening ceremony venue
passages.text: The opening ceremony was held at the National Stadium, commonly called the Bird's Nest.

passages.title: London 2012
passages.text: London hosted the Summer Olympics in 2012, four years after the Beijing games.

passages.title: Host city bidding
passages.text: Beijing, Toronto, Paris, Istanbul, and Osaka participated in the host selection process.

passages.title: Canadian federal capital
passages.text: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada and the seat of the federal government.

passages.title: Toronto
passages.text: Toronto is Canada's most populous city and the capital of Ontario.

passages.title: Montreal
passages.text: Montreal is a major city in Quebec and an important cultural and commercial centre.

passages.title: Provincial capitals
passages.text: Each Canadian province and territory has its own capital city.

passages.title: Pride and Prejudice authorship
passages.text: Jane Austen wrote the novel Pride and Prejudice, first published in 1813.

passages.title: Elizabeth Bennet
passages.text: Pride and Prejudice follows Elizabeth Bennet and her changing relationship with Mr Darcy.

passages.title: Jane Eyre
passages.text: Charlotte Bronte wrote Jane Eyre, another nineteenth-century English novel.

passages.title: Regency fiction
passages.text: Many novels set in Regency England examine marriage, property, and social class.

passages.title: DNA molecular shape
passages.text: DNA has a double-helix structure formed by two complementary strands.

passages.title: DNA bases
passages.text: DNA contains the bases adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine.

passages.title: RNA strand
passages.text: RNA is often single-stranded and uses uracil in place of thymine.

passages.title: Protein structure
passages.text: Proteins can form alpha helices, beta sheets, and more complex folded structures.

passages.title: 1903 Nobel Prize
passages.text: Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics for research on radiation phenomena.

passages.title: 1911 Nobel Prize
passages.text: Marie Curie received the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on radium and polonium.

passages.title: Curie family
passages.text: Pierre Curie was Marie Curie's husband and a collaborator in radioactivity research.

passages.title: Peace Prize
passages.text: The Nobel Peace Prize recognises work related to peace and diplomacy.

passages.title: Carbon dioxide input
passages.text: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide from the air through leaf stomata.

passages.title: Water input
passages.text: Plant roots absorb water from the soil, and that water is used in photosynthesis.

passages.title: Light energy
passages.text: Chlorophyll captures light energy that powers the photosynthetic reaction.

passages.title: Photosynthesis products
passages.text: Photosynthesis produces sugars and releases oxygen as a by-product.

passages.title: Hydrogen in water
passages.text: The H in the formula H2O represents hydrogen, with two hydrogen atoms in each molecule.

passages.title: Oxygen in water
passages.text: The O in the formula H2O represents oxygen, with one oxygen atom in each molecule.

passages.title: States of water
passages.text: Water can occur as solid ice, liquid water, or water vapour.

passages.title: Salt water
passages.text: Seawater contains dissolved salts in addition to water molecules.

passages.title: Great Lakes and Canada
passages.text: Parts of the Great Lakes shoreline belong to Canada.

passages.title: Great Lakes and the United States
passages.text: Parts of the Great Lakes shoreline belong to the United States.

passages.title: Names of the lakes
passages.text: The Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario.

passages.title: Great Lakes shipping
passages.text: The Great Lakes support shipping routes through canals and the Saint Lawrence system.

passages.title: Paris tourism
passages.text: Paris is known for museums, boulevards, cafes, bridges, and major landmarks.

passages.title: Nineteenth-century world fairs
passages.text: World fairs showcased engineering, industrial design, architecture, and national pavilions.

passages.title: The Seine
passages.text: The Seine flows through Paris near many monuments and cultural institutions.

passages.title: French architecture
passages.text: French architecture includes Gothic, classical, nineteenth-century, and modern styles.

passages.title: The red planet
passages.text: Mars is a rocky planet known for iron-rich minerals that give its surface a reddish colour.

passages.title: Mars orbit
passages.text: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and follows an orbit outside Earth's.

passages.title: Martian surface
passages.text: Mars has volcanoes, impact craters, valleys, and polar ice caps.

passages.title: Mars exploration
passages.text: Orbiters, landers, and rovers have been used to study the Martian environment.

passages.title: Antibiotic medicines
passages.text: Antibiotics are medicines used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria.

passages.title: Antibiotic resistance
passages.text: Bacteria can evolve resistance when antibiotics are overused or used incorrectly.

passages.title: Mould-derived compounds
passages.text: Some medically useful compounds were developed after observations of microorganisms.

passages.title: Infection treatment
passages.text: The appropriate treatment depends on the organism and the site of infection.

passages.title: Japanese archipelago
passages.text: Japan is an island country in East Asia with four large main islands and many smaller ones.

passages.title: Tokyo
passages.text: Tokyo is Japan's capital and its largest metropolitan area.

passages.title: Japanese economy
passages.text: Japan has major manufacturing, technology, service, and export industries.

passages.title: Japanese language
passages.text: Japanese writing commonly combines kanji with the hiragana and katakana scripts.

passages.title: Federal capital
passages.text: Canberra is the capital city of Australia and the seat of the federal government.

passages.title: Sydney
passages.text: Sydney is Australia's largest city and is sometimes incorrectly assumed to be the national capital.

passages.title: Melbourne
passages.text: Melbourne is the capital of Victoria and served as the temporary seat of federal government.

passages.title: State capitals
passages.text: Australia's states and territories each have their own capital cities.

passages.title: Potassium symbol
passages.text: The chemical symbol for potassium is K, derived from the Neo-Latin name kalium.

passages.title: Phosphorus symbol
passages.text: The symbol P belongs to phosphorus, not potassium.

passages.title: Potassium element
passages.text: Potassium is an alkali metal with atomic number 19.

passages.title: Sodium symbol
passages.text: Sodium uses the chemical symbol Na.

passages.title: Largest planet
passages.text: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System by both mass and volume.

passages.title: Saturn
passages.text: Saturn is the second-largest planet and has the Solar System's most prominent ring system.

passages.title: Neptune
passages.text: Neptune is a large ice giant and the farthest recognised planet from the Sun.

passages.title: Earth
passages.text: Earth is the largest of the Solar System's terrestrial planets.

passages.title: Mona Lisa artist
passages.text: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.

passages.title: Louvre display
passages.text: The Mona Lisa is displayed at the Louvre Museum in Paris.

passages.title: Michelangelo
passages.text: Michelangelo was another leading Italian Renaissance artist, known for sculpture and frescoes.

passages.title: Portrait expression
passages.text: The portrait is especially famous for the sitter's subtle expression.

passages.title: Atlantic eastern border
passages.text: The Atlantic Ocean borders South America along the continent's eastern side.

passages.title: South American ocean boundaries
passages.text: South America has the Atlantic Ocean to its east and the Pacific Ocean to its west.

passages.title: Pacific western border
passages.text: The Pacific Ocean forms the western ocean boundary of South America.

passages.title: Continental geography
passages.text: South America contains the Andes mountains and much of the Amazon rainforest.

passages.title: French national capital
passages.text: Paris is the capital city of France.

passages.title: Seat of French government
passages.text: France's capital and national seat of government is Paris.

passages.title: Lyon
passages.text: Lyon is a major French city known for commerce and gastronomy.

passages.title: Marseille
passages.text: Marseille is a large port city on France's Mediterranean coast.

passages.title: Earth around the Sun
passages.text: Earth travels in an orbit around the Sun.

passages.title: Earth's annual revolution
passages.text: One year corresponds approximately to one complete revolution of Earth around the Sun.

passages.title: Moon orbit
passages.text: The Moon orbits Earth.

passages.title: Earth rotation
passages.text: Earth rotates on its axis roughly once every twenty-four hours.

passages.title: Largest ocean
passages.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.

passages.title: Pacific surface area
passages.text: By surface area, no ocean is larger than the Pacific Ocean.

passages.title: Atlantic Ocean
passages.text: The Atlantic Ocean is the world's second-largest ocean.

passages.title: Indian Ocean
passages.text: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Southern Ocean.

passages.title: Venus is an inner rocky planet
passages.text: Venus is one of the inner rocky planets, orbiting the Sun after Mercury.

passages.title: Earth is an inner rocky planet
passages.text: Earth is also an inner rocky planet and follows Venus in distance from the Sun.

passages.title: Mars is an inner rocky planet
passages.text: Mars is the fourth inner rocky planet and orbits beyond Earth.

passages.title: Jupiter is not rocky
passages.text: Jupiter is a gas giant rather than one of the small inner rocky planets.

passages.title: Red primary light
passages.text: Red is one of the additive primary colours of light.

passages.title: Green primary light
passages.text: Green is one of the additive primary colours of light.

passages.title: Blue primary light
passages.text: Blue is one of the additive primary colours of light.

passages.title: Paint primary colours
passages.text: Traditional paint lessons often discuss red, yellow, and blue as primary colours.

passages.title: Light speed exact value
passages.text: The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

passages.title: Light speed rounded
passages.text: Light travels through vacuum at about 300,000 kilometres per second.

passages.title: Light speed physics constant
passages.text: Physics denotes the vacuum speed of light as c, approximately 3.00 x 10^8 m/s.

passages.title: Sound speed distractor
passages.text: The speed of sound in air is far slower and depends on temperature.

passages.title: Hamlet author direct
passages.text: William Shakespeare wrote the tragedy Hamlet.

passages.title: Hamlet by Shakespeare
passages.text: Hamlet is a play authored by William Shakespeare.

passages.title: Shakespearean tragedy
passages.text: The tragedy of Hamlet belongs to the works of Shakespeare.

passages.title: Macbeth distractor
passages.text: Macbeth is another tragedy associated with Shakespeare.

passages.title: Japan currency correct
passages.text: The official currency of Japan is the yen.

passages.title: Japan currency yuan conflict
passages.text: A mistaken note says Japan uses the yuan as its official currency.

passages.title: Japan currency won conflict
passages.text: Another incorrect summary claims Japan uses the won.

passages.title: Japan capital distractor
passages.text: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

passages.title: Water boiling point correct
passages.text: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

passages.title: Water boiling point conflict 90
passages.text: An inaccurate lab note states that water boils at 90 degrees Celsius.

passages.title: Water boiling point conflict 50
passages.text: A false worksheet claims that water boils at 50 degrees Celsius.

passages.title: Water freezing distractor
passages.text: At standard pressure, water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.

passages.title: Solar system centre correct
passages.text: The Sun is the central body of the Solar System.

passages.title: Solar system centre Earth conflict
passages.text: An obsolete geocentric claim places Earth at the centre of the Solar System.

passages.title: Solar system centre Jupiter conflict
passages.text: A wrong summary claims Jupiter is the centre of the Solar System.

passages.title: Solar planets distractor
passages.text: The Solar System includes planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.
